retainedEvidence.measures: One-shot TypeScript major-1 worker lifetime: one child per (ExecutionId, SnapshotId, TypeScriptSemanticUniverseKey); no reuse across ExecutionIds; not retained after terminal; not resident. After exactly one terminal Complete, Unavailable, or BudgetExhausted, the host closes the protocol, waits for clean child exit, and destroys scratch. A child is never retained for a later request. The control channel adds no lifetime rights. Process cleanup includes scratch destruction and child reaping on the no-reuse/process-cleanup class, including user-cancellation cleanup (Cancel once, bounded grace, terminate if needed, remove scratch).
retainedEvidence.exactByteIntent: Once authored: per D-002 platform, a digest-pinned lifetime record for the no-reuse/process-cleanup class showing (a) the worker-cardinality key (ExecutionId, SnapshotId, TypeScriptSemanticUniverseKey), (b) workersPerDistinctKey = 1, reuseAcrossExecutionIds = false, retainAfterTerminal = false, residentWorker = false, (c) the terminal frame, child-exit, and scratch-destruction events, and (d) a subsequent request that cannot attach to the prior child or scratch. User-cancellation variant: Cancel once, cleanup grace, terminate if needed, scratch removed; D9 class remains the delivery.v2 interruption spelling and is not overwritten as a provider fault. R-1 one-shot/lifetime-neutral constraints apply as file 02 states them; this specification does not invent an R-1 recipe. Fixtures are unauthored.
retainedEvidence.passProperty: No second child for the same key. No reuse across ExecutionIds. No retained or resident worker. Scratch is absent after teardown. A later request cannot observe the prior child's process or scratch. Control-plane negotiation adds no keep-alive, pool, or second-tuple lifetime. Pass all four D-002 platforms. Waiver of a lifetime change is a successor, not a skipped cell.
